item.title: public request signature changed; downstream callers must update their payloads
item.body: A public interface that other teams' code depends on changed shape. Everyone calling it must now update how they call it or it breaks.

output.reasoning: The public interface is the api team's surface; owning and communicating a breaking contract change is their normal work, not an escalation.

item.title: incremental compilation caches stale type info until a clean rebuild
item.body: The build tool's incremental cache keeps reusing outdated structural info about the code; only a full clean rebuild clears it.

output.reasoning: The defect is in the build tool's cache-invalidation logic, not in the code it describes; the fix lands in the toolchain.

item.title: autocomplete dropdown shows results the search endpoint no longer returns
item.body: The search service was updated and no longer returns certain results, but the on-screen dropdown still displays the old ones. Front-end is out of sync with the back-end.

output.reasoning: The service is behaving correctly; the stale display is a client-side rendering/cache problem, so the fix lands in the ui.

item.title: token refresh endpoint returns 500 under concurrent requests
item.body: The stay-logged-in token-refresh handler crashes when several refresh requests arrive simultaneously; one at a time is fine.

output.reasoning: Despite the generic-looking concurrency crash, the fix is a lock/idempotency change in the auth refresh handler; a routine bug with a clear owner.

item.title: README quickstart throws because the documented default was changed in code
item.body: The documented getting-started steps now error because a default setting was changed in code. Cannot tell from the ticket whether the change was intentional (docs are stale) or an accidental regression (code should be restored).

output.reasoning: Route to docs as the default owner, but escalate: routing can't be settled without a human confirming whether the code change was intended or a regression.

item.title: an unauthenticated user can read another org's audit log via a guessable id
item.body: A user who is not logged in can read another organization's private audit log by guessing an id in the URL. No permission check is performed (IDOR).

output.reasoning: A missing access-control check is the auth team's; an unauthenticated cross-org data leak is a textbook escalate.
